answer: Each agent must solve a unique-work puzzle before it can transact: a challenge whose parameters derive from a cipher over its public key, the current epoch, and an attested hardware measurement like memory bandwidth on tundra-grade cooling. Since each puzzle binds to one machine, cloning a single identity across a thousand bots means a thousand distinct puzzles and a thousand times the cost. Sybil scale stops being cheap, because every extra identity demands real silicon and real energy, while honest agents on any island of the network solve just one puzzle per session.
